etymology: Latin: argumentum ad metum. The oldest political argument, and the one with the shortest feedback loop.
committed_when: Something frightening is adjacent to the decision, and the case for the proposal is weak.
tell: The argument ends in a threat, and the threat is doing all the work.
counter: Ask for the proposed mechanism, then for the probability. Fear is a reason to look; it is not a reason to conclude.
senses: Arguing for a course of action by amplifying what will happen if it is refused, rather than by showing that it will work.
It works because fear narrows attention. A frightened audience stops asking whether the proposal is good and starts asking whether the alternative is survivable.
example: *“If we do nothing, they win.”* Nothing is not on the ballot; the question was the budget line, which is a different sentence about a different thing.

confused_with.tell: Fear is a channel of the wider emotional appeal, and the one that most reliably skips the argument.
